business_process: Train dispatching and movement authority on company track
description: Issue and cancel track warrants; check conflicts; grant maintenance-of-way track and time; publish speed restrictions and bulletins; keep train sheets and the radio log
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Every movement on 186 route miles needs a track warrant. Manual dispatch can keep about half of normal train starts running, but raises the chance of a conflicting authority (P01 R-005). After 24 hours the railroad must hold PIH and most other trains; about $117,000 revenue per operating day. Active authorities change minute to minute, so no more than 1 hour of CAD data may be lost; anything newer is rebuilt by radio roll call
manual_workaround: Paper track warrant procedure with repeat-back (2019 version; update and drill due 2026-12-31); train sheets printed each shift; printed track chart and bulletin list at each console; paper radio log
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-04 (dispatch VLAN; radio gateway and consoles; tower sites); SYS-05; SYS-07; SYS-08 (operations workstations); SYS-09 (backup vault)
dependent_third_parties: Dispatch system vendor; MSP; radio equipment vendor; microwave and cellular carriers
dependent_people_or_facilities: 6 train dispatchers and the Chief Dispatcher (24/7); HQ dispatch center; 7 tower sites

description: Call crews with required rest; record on-duty time; deliver bulletins and train lists to crews on rugged tablets
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: No train runs without a rested, called crew. Crews and callers can work from paper for one day; after that the risk of hours-of-service recording errors and missed calls grows. Crew records are entered through the day, so 4 hours of loss can be rebuilt from paper sign-in sheets
manual_workaround: Phone calling from a printed crew board refreshed each shift; paper on-duty forms keyed in later; paper bulletins handed out at the yard offices
dependent_systems: SYS-09 (crew management and hours-of-service application); SYS-08 (crew tablets); SYS-05; SYS-06
dependent_third_parties: Public cloud provider; MSP; cellular carrier
dependent_people_or_facilities: Crew callers at dispatch; 92 train and engine employees; Central, North, and South Yard offices

business_process: Interchange service over the Class I trackage-rights segment (PTC tenant operations)
description: Run 2 to 3 interchange trains a day over 26 miles of the Class I's PTC-equipped main line; initialize onboard PTC with current locomotive, crew, and consist data; report en route PTC failures to the host
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: All carloads reach the national network through this interchange. No company train may enter the segment without an operative onboard PTC apparatus (49 CFR 236.1006(a)). After 48 hours cars back up at Central Yard and in the Class I's yard, and the Class I and shippers begin embargoes. The consist feeding PTC initialization comes from the TMS; losing more than 4 hours of consist changes forces a manual re-check of every car
manual_workaround: Hold interchange traffic at Central Yard; ask the Class I to move interchange cars with its own crews (not yet agreed; P01 R-013); rebuild consists from the daily TMS export and a car-by-car walk
dependent_systems: SYS-02 (onboard units; PTC administration workstation; vendor-hosted PTC back office); SYS-03; SYS-05; SYS-01
dependent_third_parties: PTC back office vendor; Class I host railroad; industry interoperable messaging network
dependent_people_or_facilities: 8 PTC-equipped road locomotives; interchange crews; Car Management and Customer Service Manager

business_process: Car management, waybilling, interchange reporting, and billing
description: Create waybills; track car location; send and receive interchange EDI; bill freight and demurrage
process_owner: Car Management and Customer Service Manager
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Cars can move for up to 3 days on paper waybills and the daily consist export, but the Class I needs EDI to accept cars in normal volume. Billing can wait for the next invoice cycle. The TMS is SaaS; the daily export sets a 24-hour RPO for the company's own copy
manual_workaround: Paper waybills; daily consist export on the file server; phone and email to the Class I car desk; invoices delayed
dependent_third_parties: TMS vendor; Class I car desk; EDI network provider
dependent_people_or_facilities: 5 car management and customer service clerks

business_process: Track, bridge, and signal inspection and maintenance
description: Required track and bridge inspections by designated inspectors (49 CFR 213.7; 213.233); maintenance-of-way work planning; inspection records; the AI defect detection pilot
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Inspections are visual and continue on paper; only record keeping and planning depend on IT. Work authority comes from dispatch (BP-01). Records are saved daily
manual_workaround: Paper inspection forms entered later; work authority by radio under manual dispatch; the AI pilot is simply paused (it only supplements visual inspection)
dependent_systems: SYS-06; SYS-08; SYS-09 (inspection records); SYS-11 (pilot, not required)
dependent_third_parties: AI pilot vendor (not required for recovery)
dependent_people_or_facilities: 58 maintenance-of-way and 14 signal and communications employees; qualified track inspectors

business_process: Wayside detector and grade crossing health monitoring
description: Relay hot bearing and dragging equipment detector alarms and crossing remote health monitor alarms to the dispatch center so dispatchers can stop trains or protect crossings
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Detectors also announce by radio to the passing train, and crossing warning circuits work on their own. But the 14 monitored crossings report malfunctions only through the network; without it a failed crossing may go unnoticed until a crew reports it. Configuration and alarm history are saved daily
manual_workaround: Train crews report crossing problems by radio; signal maintainers patrol the 14 monitored crossings; dispatcher issues protection instructions for any crossing reported faulty
dependent_systems: SYS-04 (detectors; crossing monitors; cellular modems); SYS-01 (alarm display); SYS-07
dependent_third_parties: Cellular carrier; detector and crossing monitor vendors

description: Schedule trucks; transfer lumber, fertilizer, and feed between rail cars and trucks; issue bills of lading
process_owner: Car Management and Customer Service Manager
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Truck customers can be scheduled by phone for several days; after 3 days transload volume and revenue fall. Data is saved daily
manual_workaround: Phone scheduling; paper bills of lading

business_process: Locomotive and car mechanical, including onboard PTC maintenance
description: Inspect and repair locomotives and cars; pull onboard PTC logs; keep onboard units operative and sealed
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Inspections continue on paper. Onboard PTC troubleshooting needs the PTC administration workstation, but the 8 equipped locomotives can keep running while their units stay operative. Records are saved daily
manual_workaround: Paper inspection and repair forms; defer non-urgent onboard PTC log pulls
dependent_systems: SYS-02 (PTC administration workstation); SYS-06; SYS-08 (shop PCs)
dependent_third_parties: PTC back office vendor; parts suppliers

description: Answer TSA requests for RSSM car location within 30 minutes (49 CFR 1580.203(d)); keep chain-of-custody records (1580.205); report significant security concerns, including cyber attacks, to TSA within 24 hours (1570.203); keep Security Coordinators reachable (1570.201); protect SSI
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: A TSA location request can come at any hour and must be answered within 30 minutes, even during an IT outage. So the fallback must always be ready, not recovered. The printed RSSM car list is refreshed every 4 hours, which sets the RPO
manual_workaround: Printed RSSM car list at the dispatch center every 4 hours; clean standby laptop with cellular access to the TMS; paper chain-of-custody forms; TSOC reporting by telephone
dependent_systems: SYS-03; SYS-06 (SSI library); SYS-08 (standby laptop); dispatch center telephones
dependent_third_parties: TMS vendor; TSA Transportation Security Operations Center (TSOC)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Manager of Safety and Security (primary Security Coordinator); Chief Dispatcher (alternate); dispatch center

description: Pay employees; onboard and terminate; accounts payable and receivable
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll runs every two weeks. A missed payroll has legal and labor relations impact, but the prior run can be repeated
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll through the payroll provider; manual payments by bank portal with call-back verification
dependent_third_parties: Payroll and HR SaaS vendor; bank
